# Copilot instructions for this repository

## Project overview

This repository is a Vite + React + TypeScript personal blog/site, served as a static GitHub Pages app. The app is intentionally split between a landing/home experience and a blog section:

- `src/App.tsx` defines the app routes and uses `HashRouter` instead of `BrowserRouter` because the site is published on GitHub Pages.
- `src/components/Home.tsx` renders the landing page and lazy-loads the 3D scene.
- `src/components/PostList.tsx` and `src/components/PostDetails.tsx` render the blog index and each post page.
- Blog content lives in `src/posts/*.md`; each file is treated as a route slug based on its filename.
- `scripts/generate-posts-index.mjs` scans `src/posts`, reads frontmatter metadata, and regenerates `src/posts-index.json` before dev/build. This file is the source of the blog index and post sorting.
- Styling is Tailwind-based (`vite.config.ts` includes `@tailwindcss/vite`), while the site also renders Markdown with `react-markdown`, `remark-gfm`, `remark-math`, and `rehype-katex`.

## Build, lint, and validation commands

Use `pnpm` for package management and scripts:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run dev
pnpm run build
pnpm run lint
pnpm run normalize-posts
pnpm run deploy
```

Important script behavior:

- `pnpm run dev` starts the Vite dev server for local development.
- `pnpm run build` creates the production build in `dist`.
- `pnpm run lint` runs ESLint (`eslint.config.js`).
- `pnpm run normalize-posts` updates frontmatter and regenerates the blog index; it is used in deployment prep.
- `pnpm run predeploy` runs normalization and the production build before `pnpm run deploy`, which publishes `dist` via `gh-pages`.

There is no automated test suite checked into this repo right now. Validation is primarily via `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run build`.

## High-value conventions specific to this repo

### Markdown posts are the content source

- Every blog post is a file under `src/posts/`.
- The filename becomes the route slug, so keep the slug stable when moving content.
- Posts use YAML frontmatter at the top, typically including `title`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`, with dates formatted as `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- Post cards display `updated_at`, falling back to `created_at` when no update date is set.
- `PostDetails.tsx` lazily loads Markdown with `import.meta.glob("/src/posts/*.md", { query: "?raw", import: "default" })` and strips frontmatter before rendering.
- Do not manually edit `src/posts-index.json`; it is generated by `scripts/generate-posts-index.mjs`.

### GitHub Pages constraints matter

- The site uses a hash-based route (`HashRouter`) rather than browser history, which is important for static hosting.
- Keep links consistent with `#/blog/...` route expectations when referencing blog entries.

### Performance and loading patterns are intentional

- The homepage 3D scene is lazy-loaded (`React.lazy`) because it is heavy.
- Blog routes are also lazy-loaded in `src/App.tsx` to keep the initial app shell light.
- `vite.config.ts` creates separate vendor chunks for Three.js and Markdown tooling to avoid one oversized bundle.

### Content and metadata are generated, not hand-maintained

- `generate-posts-index.mjs` derives a post title fallback from the filename, sorts posts by `updated_at` (falling back to `created_at`), and writes both timestamps to `src/posts-index.json`.
- When renaming posts, the script attempts to preserve title metadata by comparing old tracked versions in Git.
- The post detail page derives meta descriptions from Markdown content via `toExcerpt()`.

## Repository-specific notes

- `README.md` is intentionally minimal; this project is a personal website rather than a multi-package app.
- `dist/` is generated output, not source code.
- `public/` contains static assets distributed without bundling.
- The app is content-heavy but not framework-heavy: most behavior is in routed components plus generated post metadata rather than a large state store.

## When changing content or routes

- Prefer updating the Markdown file itself instead of hardcoding post details elsewhere.
- If you add or rename a post, regenerate the index with `pnpm run normalize-posts` to keep the blog list and dates in sync.
- Keep route slugs aligned with filenames and ensure the file still includes valid frontmatter for title and timestamp metadata.
